items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: he was in the family too, it was another band I played in, we had a traditional jazz band.

ctx.x: RPI. I have an uncle who is still living, Gilley Roberts, he’s a banjo player who played with Louis Armstrong in 1927, and went to Europe with him and everything. Gilley is 104. And one of my other jobs, he was in the family too, it was another band I played in, we had a traditional jazz band. And we worked all the colleges, like all the fancy colleges, Amherst and University of Massachusetts and all the Upstate schools, and just playing trad music. And this was like in the fifties. And we would make like…
They kept a tight— right. Well best of luck.
